title: New National Electricity Policy: what it could mean for your power bill
dek: A draft policy to replace the 2005 rules proposes yearly automatic tariff increases and cutting cross-subsidies.
seoTitle: Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 explained: tariffs, subsidies, timeline
bigLabel: Per-person electricity use the draft policy targets

glance.what: The Power Ministry released a draft National Electricity Policy in January 2026 to replace the 2005 policy. Public comments closed on 19 February.
glance.why: It proposes index-linked tariff increases every April and limits on cross-subsidies, which could change household and industrial power bills.
glance.next: The final policy has to be notified. Nothing in the draft applies until then.

forYou: Under the draft, tariffs would rise each April by an index rather than waiting for state regulators, and free power would need the subsidy paid to discoms in advance.

events.title: Draft policy released for consultation
events.summary: It proposes automatic yearly tariff revisions, no tariff below 50% of the average cost of supply, and exempting manufacturing and railways from cross-subsidy charges.

events.title: Public comment period closes
events.summary: Stakeholders had until 19 February to send comments. Kerala media highlighted that power bills would rise automatically every 1 April under the draft.
